title: Historic Deal Positions FIA World Endurance Championship for Record Decade of Growth as the Sport Enters its Golden Age
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), the founder and organiser of the 24 Hours of Le Mans, have today announced a major deal for the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), securing another decade of growth.   The landmark agreement, which comes during a period of unprecedented growth for the championship, will ensure a common ambition to expand the partnership and drive its commercial success. It will run from the end of 2027, when the current agreement expires, to the end of 2037.    Under the extended partnership agreement, all regulatory processes will be overseen by FIA Working Groups, the FIA Endurance Commission, and will require the final approval of the FIA World Motor Sport Council. The homologation process has also been streamlined, with the FIA and ACO overseeing the homologation of all cars competing in the Hypercar class.   The renewed partnership will also deliver significantly increased branding for the FIA. This includes enhanced branding prominently displayed across key areas including parc fermé, the podium and the Safety Cars, as well as across broadcast coverage.   With an expanding fanbase, a wider pool of competitors, and a global calendar of iconic events, the championship is stronger than ever. Since its inception in 2012, it has set the global standard for long-distance circuit racing. Following the introduction of the Hypercar regulations in 2021, interest in the championship from motor sport fans and from the automotive world has surged.    FIA WEC’s trackside audience has grown 8% so far in 2026, with millions of fans following the championship globally. The fanbase for the championship is also evolving. This year, 44% of attendees are aged 34 or younger, while 40% are attending an FIA WEC event for the first time. The championship has secured the long-term loyalty of its existing fanbase, while building the next generation of endurance racing fans.   Eight of the world’s leading auto-manufacturers currently compete in Hypercar, the top category of FIA WEC. Following the addition of the LMGT3 class in 2024, the championship now counts no fewer than 14 marques in total on the starting grid. Two more giants of the automotive industry – Ford and McLaren – are set to join the Hypercar ranks in 2027.   For over 100 years, endurance racing has served as a proven testbed for technologies that transfer from track to road. This renewed agreement creates a solid framework for advancing hydrogen powertrains in competition, providing a clear pathway toward more sustainable transport and mobility.    It will also deliver a more unified technical framework that defines top-level endurance racing Hypercars competing both in the FIA WEC and IMSA in North America, which will be introduced from 2030.  The new framework will provide greater cost-efficiency for manufacturers to compete in endurance racing championships and events globally, boosting potential participation and increasing the spectacle for motor sport fans.   With interest in FIA WEC at levels never seen before, the championship is positioned for continued growth and success over the coming decade. This new deal offers the solid foundation needed to secure its future, marking a milestone moment in the history of FIA WEC.    Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA , said:  “This is not simply an agreement, it is a vital step forward for racing that will secure the future of the FIA World Endurance Championship for years to come.     “This is a deal built for the future, a deal of the century, one that strengthens the collaboration between the FIA and ACO, a relationship that dates back over 120 years, and sets the championship up for a decade of record growth that will deliver real benefits to fans, drivers, teams and manufacturers.     “It has been an honour to play a part in the collaboration that has helped usher in this golden age of endurance racing. I look forward to continuing our work alongside President Pierre Fillon and his team as we build on this momentum and shape an even stronger future.”     Pierre Fillon, President of the Automobile Club de l'Ouest , said: “ We are delighted to see the agreement between the FIA and the ACO extended, reinforcing the strong and long-standing relationship that has been at the heart of the FIA World Endurance Championship since its creation in 2012. This partnership has been built on trust, shared ambition, and a common commitment to the development of endurance racing.      “Together, the FIA and the ACO have created a solid foundation for the continued success and international growth of the championship, and we look forward to writing the next chapter of this remarkable collaboration. Finally, I would like to thank FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem for the great relationship we have built.”      Alberto Villarreal, General Manager at the FIA , said:  “The FIA World Endurance Championship is stronger and more popular than it has ever been before, with a growing and evolving fanbase, and an impressive roster of top-tier global auto-manufacturers.      “The agreement announced today underlines the investment in the championship from both the FIA and the ACO, and our commitment to continue bringing the sport to new audiences. It is a pivotal moment in the history of FIA WEC, and provides the foundation and stability needed for the championship’s ongoing success.”      Frédéric Lequien, CEO of the Le Mans Endurance Management, the promoter for the FIA World Endurance Championship , said:  “This agreement comes at an exciting time for the FIA World Endurance Championship. The championship is experiencing exceptional momentum, with growing engagement from manufacturers, teams, partners, media, and fans around the world. The extension provides a strong framework to build on this growth, further strengthen the global appeal of the WEC and continue to deliver a world-class championship at the forefront of endurance racing. We are looking forward to an ambitious and exciting future for the FIA WEC.”     -   Notes to Editors     The renewed agreement between the FIA and the ACO follows three other significant long-term agreement announcements since July 2025:      FIA and Formula E sign landmark extension to power Formula E World Championship for another 10 years, announced in July 2025 –  information here        Multi-year Concorde Governance Agreement between the FIA, Formula 1 Group and all 11 race teams, announced in December 2025 –  information here        “Deal of the Century” for FIA World and European Rally Championships in July 2026 –  information here         These announcements form part of the FIA’s strategic investment in the future of motor sport, as it continues its mission to grow participation in the sport and provide a safe and accessible platform for all.      The FIA has seen a radical transformation since 2021, and earlier this year  announced  that it had delivered its strongest set of financial results in a decade in 2025, with an operating profit of €6.7m. It also reported an exceptional gain of €20m through the Formula E contract extension.    About the FIA  The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) is the governing body for world motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations globally. It is a non-profit organisation committed to driving innovation and championing safety, sustainability and equality across motor sport and mobility.   Founded in 1904, with offices in Paris, London and Geneva, the FIA brings together 246 Member Organisations across five continents, representing millions of road users, motor sport professionals and volunteers. It develops and enforces regulations for motor sport, including six FIA World Championships, to ensure worldwide competitions are safe and fair for all.    About the ACO   Founded in 1906, the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO) is the creator and organiser of major motorsport events: the first Grand Prix in history in 1906, followed by the 24 Hours of Le Mans starting in 1923. The ACO has also been the organiser and promoter of the FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC) since 2012 and the creator of continental series: the European Le Mans Series (2004) and the Asian Le Mans Series (2013). The ACO organises the 24 Hours of Le Mans Motorcycle Race, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Karting, the 24 Hours of Le Mans Truck Race, and the French Motorcycle Grand Prix on its Le Mans circuits…   The 24 Hours of Le Mans serves as a true technological laboratory focused on automotive innovation. It is in this spirit that the ACO continues to evolve. Sustainable mobility - embodied in particular by MissionH24, which aims to introduce hydrogen to the 24 Hours of Le Mans - is a key objective for the ACO.   Since 2024, the ACO has held the FIA’s 3-star environmental accreditation and is ISO 20121 certified, the benchmark for responsible event management. In September 2024, the 24 Hours of Le Mans circuit was also voted “France’s Favourite Monument.”    About FIA WEC  The FIA World Endurance Championship (FIA WEC), created in 2012 by the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) and the Automobile Club de l’Ouest (ACO), represents the undisputed pinnacle of the long-distance discipline.   Bringing together the world’s leading manufacturers, biggest brands, top drivers and most successful teams, FIA WEC races around the globe, pushing the limits of speed, performance and durability while encouraging ever-greater feats of strategic skill. If the fast and fearless drivers are the heroes, then the cars are the stars, from their cutting-edge technology to their dynamic design. And then, of course, there is the sound of the engines – that uncompromising, unadulterated roar.   The cornerstone of the calendar is the iconic 24 Hours of Le Mans, an event born in 1923 that continues to serve as the ultimate test for manufacturers seeking to prove their mettle – but every race has its own character, challenges and pitfalls. As a series with a proud history, a compelling present and a thrilling future, FIA WEC remains endurance racing’s global benchmark, continuously setting the standard in the sport and inspiring generations to come. title: Bigger and even better FIA FREC calendar for 2027
summary: Sport news The FIA Formula Regional European Championship will be contested over 10 events in 2027 with a round supporting the FIA Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix*, plus the addition of Barcelona, Portimão and Silverstone to the schedule, among the key highlights.   Following FIA World Motor Sport Council approval, it is confirmed that the race for success in year two of FIA FREC will begin at Autodromo do Algarve in Portimão from 8-11 April, one of six venues due to appear on the FIA Formula One World Championship calendar next season.   Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, which along with Portimão and Silverstone is a newcomer to the FIA FREC schedule, is set to host the season finale from 7-10 October and bring the curtain down on an expanded calendar, which has increased to 10 rounds after eight rounds took place in 2026.   Organised and promoted by FIA Member Club Automobile Club d’Italia (ACI), FIA FREC enjoys the full support of the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile, the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide. It follows Formula 4 on the FIA Single-Seater Pyramid with FIA Formula 3 the next step ahead of FIA Formula 2 and FIA Formula 1.   Formula 1 drivers Kimi Antonelli, Gabriel Bortoleto, Franco Colapinto and Isack Hadjar are all graduates of Formula Regional while several drivers who raced in FIA FREC in 2026 did so with the support of Formula 1 team academies.   In another change for 2027, all events will include a maximum of two races after some rounds featured three races during FIA FREC’s inaugural 2026 season.   With the exception of the FIA Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix support event*, all FIA FREC weekends will consist of free practice on Friday, Qualifying 1 and Race 1 on Saturday and Qualifying 2 and Race 2 on Sunday.   The format of the Hungaroring weekend* is subject to confirmation but is expected to feature Free Practice and Qualifying on Friday 30 July, Race 1 on Saturday 31 July and Race 2 on Sunday 1 August.   Meanwhile, the frequency of events has been adjusted to allow a longer gap between each round. This has been achieved through an earlier start to the season and a later finish.    FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro said:   “The success of FIA FREC’s inaugural season, with 11 different winners, has given us a strong foundation for 2027. Expanding to 10 rounds responds to the wishes of the teams, while the revised weekend format and the spacing between events reflect feedback from drivers, teams and partners. While the round is subject to contract, the chance to race alongside Formula 1 at the Hungaroring will give our drivers, mechanics and engineers an invaluable opportunity to showcase their potential on one of the sport’s biggest stages.”     ACI Sport General Manager Mario Isola said :    “The FIA Formula Regional European Championship plays an important role in developing the next generation of single-seater talent. Working closely with the FIA, ACI Sport is committed to giving drivers and teams a strong sporting platform as the championship grows to 10 rounds in 2027. We are also proud that Imola and Monza, two circuits with a special place in Italian motorsport, will host the championship as part of the ACI Racing Weekends.”    The provisional FIA FREC calendar for 2027 follows**:   9-11 April: Autodromo do Algarve, Portimão (Portugal) 23-25 April: Red Bull Ring (Austria) 14-16 May: Silverstone Circuit (Great Britain) 18-20 June: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps (Belgium) 16-18 July: Circuit Paul Ricard (France) 30 July-1 August: Hungaroring (Hungary)* 6-8 August: Circuit Zandvoort (Netherlands) 10-12 September: Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari, Imola (Italy) 24-26 September: Autodromo Nazionale Monza (Italy) 8-10 October: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya (Spain)    Q&A: FIA Single-Seater Commission President Emanuele Pirro     The FIA FREC calendar for 2027 has increased from eight to 10 rounds. Why?   “It was the overwhelming wish of the teams to expand the schedule and there was plenty of interest from venue and event promoters given the success of the inaugural FIA FREC season, with 30-car grids at all events, 11 winners and great racing from potential Formula 1 world champions of the future. To accommodate more events, we’ve changed the format of the weekends by removing the reverse-grid race, so the number of races will be capped at 20, which is the same amount as originally scheduled in 2026. We’ve also worked hard on improving the frequency of events to allow for a bigger gap between each weekend, which has been done in response to feedback from our drivers, teams and partners.”     How important is the addition of a Formula 1 support race*?   “It’s really important and, equally, it’s great news. FIA FREC is the second step on the FIA Junior Single-Seater Pyramid with Formula 1 at the very top after Formula 3 and Formula 2. To compete at the highest level is an ambition of all our drivers, mechanics and engineers, so the opportunity to showcase their potential in front of Formula 1 teams cannot be underestimated. It will also be exciting for fans to experience the spectacle of FIA FREC, in many cases for the first time.”     There are some new tracks on the calendar. What benefit does this bring?   “Although consistency in the calendar is important, we also wanted to add new tracks to the season. This has been done to not only make for a level playing field, but it’s also in response from countries – and their FIA Member Clubs – that didn’t host FIA FREC events during the inaugural season in 2026. We’re delighted to be going back to seven of the eight venues we visited in 2026 but equally excited to be visiting Barcelona, Portimão and Silverstone for the first time.”          What is FIA FREC?  Having taken over from the Formula Regional European Championship by Alpine (FRECA) for the 2026 season, FIA FREC is the headlining Formula Regional Championship Certified by FIA.   All FIA FREC drivers compete in the   second-generation Formula Regional Tatuus T 326   on Pirelli tyres. Not only does the level playing field ensure close competition, it also increases the rate that drivers develop.   Developed by Italian constructor Tatuus in partnership with the FIA, the Tatuus T 326  follows the aerodynamic philosophy deployed in Formula 1 to encourage closer racing, while representing another step in terms of performance and safety. The car features the Race Mode push to pass system, which allows drivers to trigger full engine performance when activated by a button pressed from inside the cockpit. Its introduction is the result of extensive research and development managed by the FIA.   Subject to final FIA confirmation, Emanuele Olivieri is the FIA FREC champion for 2026 after he beat Sebastian Wheldon, Kean Nakamura-Berta and Rashid Al Dhaheri during a four-way title showdown at Hockenheim in Germany last month. Italian Olivieri also won the FIA FREC Rookie title, while R-ace GP from France secured the FIA FREC Teams’ title during the Hockenheim weekend.   Click   HERE   for more on the FIA Formula Regional European Championship. Watch all the FIA FREC races from 2026 on   YouTube  .    *Subject to contract   **Details of headlining/support races at all rounds to be announced in due course. title: FIA Asia Pacific Congress to Bring Member Clubs Together in the Philippines to Advance Mobility and Motor Sport Across the Region
summary: Members news    The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, will be hosted by the Automobile Association Philippines (AAP) in Boracay in the Philippines for its Asia Pacific Congress next week, bringing together FIA Member Clubs from across the region.  From 29 September to 1 October, 120 delegates from Member Clubs across Asia and the Pacific, will unite in Boracay for three days of collaboration, innovation and knowledge sharing. Throughout the week, attendees will discuss priorities to advance safe and sustainable mobility for road users and drive greater motor sport accessibility.  The Asia-Pacific region is one of the FIA's most diverse and dynamic, spanning some of the world's fastest-growing mobility markets and an expanding motor sport community. The Congress will provide Member Clubs with an opportunity to share expertise and develop practical solutions which respond to the specific needs of their members and communities.  Across mobility, discussions will focus on road safety, innovation, sustainable and accessible transport, tourism and the changing needs of road users, building on the FIA's work to support Clubs in delivering meaningful impact at a national and regional level.  Motor sport sessions will explore opportunities to increase participation, strengthen grassroots competition and create more accessible pathways into the sport, supporting the FIA's ambition to make motor sport more affordable and accessible around the world.  The programme will also showcase the work and innovation of FIA Member Clubs across Asia-Pacific, providing a platform to share successful initiatives which can be adapted and scaled across the region.   H.E. Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said:   "The Asia-Pacific region is central to the future of both mobility and motor sport, and our Member Clubs are at the heart of that progress.   From improving road safety and embracing innovation to creating new opportunities for people to participate in motor sport, our Clubs are delivering real impact for their communities.    "The FIA Asia Pacific Congress gives us an important opportunity to bring that expertise together, share ideas and strengthen collaboration across one of the most diverse and dynamic regions in our Federation.    "I thank our hosts the Automobile Association Philippines, and President Joe Ferreria, for welcoming the FIA family to Boracay and look forward to another productive Congress."    FIA Region II President and President of host club the Automobile Association Philippines, Augustus ‘Joe’ Ferreria said:   "The strength of this region comes from the diversity, knowledge and ambition of our Member Clubs. Bringing our community together in the Philippines gives us the opportunity to learn from one another, identify shared challenges and develop solutions that can support Clubs across the region.    "The Asia Pacific Congress is an important moment for us to build on the progress already being made and ensure our Clubs have the tools, knowledge and connections they need to continue growing.    "We are proud to welcome the FIA and our fellow Member Clubs from across Asia-Pacific to the Philippines.”   The Congress follows a period of significant activity for the FIA across the region.  The FIA has expanded its  Safe Mobility 4 All & 4 Life  programme into Asia-Pacific, supporting Member Clubs and authorities with training and practical tools to improve road safety, while initiatives including the  FIA Innovation Challenge  continue to showcase Club-led solutions which can be shared and scaled across the Federation.  Across motor sport, the region continues to play an important role at every level of competition, from grassroots participation and regional championships through to the FIA's major World Championships with Malaysia set to host the Bahrain Grand Prix in the days following the congress.  The FIA Member Club structure forms the backbone of the federation’s governance and operations, with each full Member Club holding voting rights across the FIA’s elections and regulatory decisions. Clubs are grouped into two primary categories, with some serving in both roles:   Mobility Clubs – provide mobility services and represent the interest of road users, with a focus on road safety, travel and tourism, consumer rights, and sustainable mobility  National Sporting Authorities (ASNs) – govern and develop motorsport at a national level, are responsible for sporting events, issuing licenses, and engagement across regulations   Within the FIA there are four Mobility Regions and 6 sport zones. The FIA Asia Pacific Congress will welcome Member Clubs from across the region. title: FIA WORLD RALLY CHAMPIONSHIP SET FOR LANDMARK EXPANSION AS U.S. AND UK RETURN TO THE CALENDAR FOR 2027
summary: Sport news The Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA), the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide, has today confirmed a landmark 15-round 2027 FIA World Rally Championship (FIA WRC) calendar, following its approval by the FIA World Motor Sport Council.  The announcement follows last week’s confirmation that Ford will return to the FIA WRC, adding to the growing momentum behind the championship as it prepares to introduce new technical regulations from 2027 and enters a new phase of commercial development under new promoter leadership.  The return of the United States and United Kingdom, together with a move to Rome for Rally d'Italia, will strengthen the championship in both important new markets and its traditional rallying heartlands, creating new opportunities to connect with fans around the world.  Rally US, scheduled for 26-29 August, will bring the championship back to the United States for the first time since 1988. Its inclusion follows a successful WRC candidate event in June 2026 and builds on the continued development of rallying in the United States.  The United Kingdom will also return to the calendar for the first time since 2019, with Rally Scotland taking place from 30 September-3 October.  Based in Aberdeen and developed by FIA Member Club Motorsport UK, the event will reconnect the FIA WRC with one of rallying’s largest and most passionate fanbases.  Rally d'Italia will provide a third major addition to the 2027 calendar, stepping up from the FIA European Rally Championship (FIA ERC) to join the FIA WRC from 8-11 July. The tarmac event will combine stages across the Lazio region with a high-profile setting in Rome, demonstrating the pathway between the FIA’s regional and world championship events.  The 2027 season will begin with its traditional opener, Rallye Monte-Carlo, from 21-24 January, before moving to two of the championship’s classic events with Rally Sweden and Safari Rally Kenya.  Croatia, the Canary Islands and Japan will then form three consecutive tarmac rounds, before Acropolis Rally Greece opens the European summer gravel sequence.  Rally d'Italia will bring a return to the tarmac of Rome in July, before Estonia and Finland place two of the championship’s fastest gravel events back-to-back, in a region where rallying enjoys exceptional levels of participation and fan support.  Both events will continue to build on alternative approaches to rally format, following the successful introduction of Estonia’s condensed programme and Finland’s fan-focused Super Sunday concept.  Following Rally US, the championship will return to Europe for Rally Scotland, before travelling to South America for rounds in Paraguay and Chile.  Before the all-important final round of the season is contested on the desert dust of Rally Saudi Arabia from 25-28 November.   Mohammed Ben Sulayem, President of the FIA, said:  “The 2027 FIA World Rally Championship calendar reflects the strong momentum behind the WRC, with new events in the United Kingdom and Italy strengthening the Championship in countries with a proud rallying heritage, while the United States gives us an exciting opportunity to grow in a country where interest in rallying continues to rise.  “With the introduction of the WRC27 technical regulations, a new promoter thanks to the deal of the century that will bring long-term investment and ambition to the championship, and a strong global calendar, the future of rallying is extremely bright.”   Éric Boullier, CEO of WRC Promoter, said:  “2027 represents the beginning of an exciting new chapter for the World Rally Championship, and this calendar reflects our ambition to build a stronger, more accessible and truly global championship.  “Returning to the United States and United Kingdom, alongside bringing the WRC to an iconic destination such as Rome, creates tremendous opportunities for our manufacturers, commercial partners and fans.  “Combined with the introduction of new technical regulations, we have a unique opportunity to shape the future of the WRC, attract new investment and bring the excitement of rallying to more people around the world.”   Julien Vial, COO of WRC Promoter, added:  “Our vision is to build a championship that combines the unique sporting challenges of rallying with world-class events capable of engaging audiences around the globe.  “This calendar strikes that balance, bringing together some of the sport's most celebrated rallies with exciting new destinations. Working closely with our organisers and partners, we want to continue raising the standard of our events and delivering an exceptional experience for fans, competitors and stakeholders.”   ENDS   For media inquiries, please contact:  Tom Wood, Head of Sport Communications: Twood@fia.com   Sven Good, Road Sport Communications Manager:  Sgood@fia.com     Notes to editors:     WRC27 technical regulations   The WRC27 regulations will come into effect from 2027, allowing both OEMs (Manufacturers) and independent tuners to design, homologate and compete with cars at the highest level of the FIA World Rally Championship.  Developed to reduce costs, broaden participation and provide long-term stability, the regulations will cap the price of a ready-to-compete WRC27 car in tarmac specification at €345,000, significantly lowering the cost of competing at the highest level of world rallying.   Ford’s return to the WRC   Ford will return to the FIA WRC with a full factory programme from 2028 and develop an all-new Rally1 car under the FIA’s new technical regulations for 2029. It becomes the fourth Constructor to commit to developing a new specification Rally1 car, joining Toyota and independent projects Project Rally One and WRT Rally1 Spain.   Candidate events   Candidate events act as test events held ahead of an event’s potential inclusion in the FIA World Rally Championship. They allow the FIA to assess whether the proposed event can meet the championship’s sporting, safety and operational requirements. Candidate events were held in the United States, United Kingdom and Rome ahead of their inclusion in the 2027 calendar.  About the FIA World Rally Championship The FIA World Rally Championship (WRC) is the ultimate test of driver skill, co-driver precision, and engineering endurance. Since its inception in 1973, WRC has pushed competitors and their cars to the limit across some of the most brutal and unforgiving terrains on the planet.  Spanning 15 rallies across five continents and 16 countries, the championship demands mastery of every surface imaginable - from snow-packed forests in sub-zero temperatures to rock-strewn mountain passes in blistering heat. Drivers and teams must adapt to ever-changing conditions as they battle against the elements and the clock.  The WRC is contested across three main titles: Drivers’ Championship, Co-Drivers’ Championship, and Manufacturers’ Championship - each requiring consistency, speed, and resilience to conquer rallying’s biggest prize.
